---
title: "Settings"
description: "Every setting of a local OmicsBase install: the .env file and the installer's variables."
---

A local install keeps its settings in `~/omicsbase/.env`. The installer writes this file the first time it runs and keeps it on every later run. You rarely need to change it.

## Change a setting {#change}

1. Open `~/omicsbase/.env` in a text editor.
2. Change the value, or remove the `#` at the start of a line to turn a setting on.
3. Apply it:

   ```bash
   cd ~/omicsbase && docker compose up -d
   ```

Make your changes only in `.env`. The other files in `~/omicsbase`, such as `docker-compose.yml` and `librechat.yaml`, are replaced each time you update, so changes there are lost.

`.env` contains secrets. The installer makes it readable only by you; keep it that way and do not share it.

## Version {#version}

| Variable | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OMICSBASE_VERSION` | `latest` | Version of the OmicsBase images (`ghcr.io/0xmuluh/omicsbase-librechat`, `-engine` and `-reports`) |

Set it to a version to stay on that version; `latest` follows the newest. To set it, run the install command with `OMICSBASE_VERSION`; see [Pin a version](updating.qmd#pin).

## Your user {#user}

| Variable | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `UID` | your user id | The user the containers run as, so files in `data/` stay yours |
| `GID` | your group id | Your group. Reports runs as another user in this group, so it can write to `data/projects` and `data/reports`. |

The installer fills these in with the output of `id -u` and `id -g`. Change them only if you move OmicsBase to another machine or user, where these ids differ. See [Move to another machine](updating.qmd#move).

## Secrets {#secrets}

| Variable | What it protects |
| --- | --- |
| `OMICSBASE_AUTH_SECRET` | Signs the tickets that let your browser into the notes engine and Reports |
| `OMICSBASE_ENGINE_SECRET` | Lets the app use the notes engine. Anyone holding it can run R on the engine. |
| `OMICSBASE_LINK_SECRET` | Between the app and the service behind **Use my own computer** |
| `MEILI_MASTER_KEY` | The search service |

The installer generates each secret once, as 32 random bytes, and keeps it on later runs. If a newer version needs a new secret, the installer adds it to your `.env`.

To write `.env` by hand without the installer, copy `.env.example` to `.env` and set each empty secret to the output of:

```bash
openssl rand -hex 32
```

When you run notes on a server, that server needs the same `OMICSBASE_ENGINE_SECRET`. See [Notes engine on a server](engine-server.qmd).

The app also generates its own sign-in keys on first start. It keeps them in `data/app/`.

## Notes engine {#engine}

| Variable | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ENGINE_URL` | not set: the engine on this machine | The HTTPS address of a notes engine on a server |

Set it to run notes' R on a bigger machine. See [Notes engine on a server](engine-server.qmd).

## Model keys {#model-keys}

| Variable | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | `user_provided` | Key for OpenAI models |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | `user_provided` | Key for Anthropic models |
| `GOOGLE_KEY` | `user_provided` | Key for Google models |

With `user_provided`, each user enters their own key in the browser when they pick a model, and it is stored encrypted for that user.

To share one key with every account on this installation, replace `user_provided` with the key, for example `OPENAI_API_KEY=<your-key>`. Every account then uses your key, and you pay for their use.

OpenRouter keys are always entered by each user in the browser. Ollama needs no key. See [Bring a model](install.qmd#step-model).

## Optional extras {#extras}

Two extras are off by default. Each is a Compose profile that you add to the start command.

### Attached-file search {#file-search}

Lets notes search the contents of attached files. The search uses embeddings, which are sent to OpenAI with the key you set here.

| Variable | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `RAG_API_URL` | not set | Address of the file-search service. Set it to `http://rag_api:8000`. |
| `RAG_OPENAI_API_KEY` | not set | OpenAI key used for the embeddings |

Remove the `#` from both lines in `.env`, set the key, then start with the profile:

```bash
cd ~/omicsbase && docker compose --profile files up -d
```

The search data is kept in `data/vectordb/`.

### Admin panel {#admin-panel}

An admin panel on <http://localhost:3000>, reachable only from this machine.

| Variable | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ADMIN_PANEL_SESSION_SECRET` | not set | Secret for the admin panel's sign-in sessions |

The installer does not generate this one. Remove the `#` from the line in `.env`, set it to the output of `openssl rand -hex 32`, then start with the profile:

```bash
cd ~/omicsbase && docker compose --profile admin up -d
```

## Install-time settings {#install-time}

These variables change what the install command does. They are not kept in `.env`. Put them before `sh` in the install command, for example:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xMuluh/omicsbase/main/install.sh | OMICSBASE_DIR=/data/omicsbase sh
```

| Variable | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OMICSBASE_DIR` | `~/omicsbase` | The folder OmicsBase is installed into. Use the same value each time you update. |
| `OMICSBASE_VERSION` | `latest` | The version to install. It is written into `.env`, also into an existing one, and the setup files are taken from that version's release (if it has none, the newest ones are used, with a note). Leave it out to keep the version already in `.env`. |
| `OMICSBASE_REF` | `main`, or the version you asked for | The branch or tag of the repository that the setup files are downloaded from. You rarely need it. |
| `OMICSBASE_EXAMPLES` | `examples-2026-11-20` | The GitHub release the example notes are downloaded from. Used only while the examples are missing. |
| `OMICSBASE_REPO` | `0xMuluh/omicsbase` | The GitHub repository the setup files and examples come from |

Several can be combined:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xMuluh/omicsbase/main/install.sh | OMICSBASE_DIR=/data/omicsbase OMICSBASE_VERSION=<version> sh
```

## Fixed settings {#fixed}

Some settings are fixed in `docker-compose.yml` and cannot be changed in `.env`:

- The ports: 3080 for the app, 3001 for Reports, 8001 for the notes engine and 3000 for the admin panel.
- Every port is reachable only from this machine.
- Sign-in is with email and password, anyone who can open the app may register, and the first account becomes the admin.
